m1.title: Arrival: your PPE
m1.desc: Put on the right protective gear and inspect an extension cord before using it.
m1.s1: Welcome to the job site! I'm Rosa, a [[journeyman]] electrician. Today you start as an [[apprentice]]. Highlighted words are what you'll hear on site: tap them to see what they mean and hear how they sound.
m1.s2: Hey, new guy! Nobody works here without [[ppe]]. Put it on now.
m1.s3: Tap each piece of your [[ppe]] to put it on: hard hat, glasses, vest, gloves and boots. Careful: not everything on the table is protective gear.
m1.wrongCap: A cap won't protect you from falling objects. On site you wear a [[hard_hat]].
m1.wrongSneakers: Sneakers don't protect against nails or impacts. You need [[work_boots]].
m1.s4: Quick question: when do you have to wear [[safety_glasses]]?
m1.s4a: Any time you're on the job site.
m1.s4aFb: Exactly. A wire clipping flying off when you cut can blind you.
m1.s4bFb: No. The person next to you is cutting and drilling too. Always on.
m1.s4c: Only when the foreman is looking.
m1.s4cFb: Your eyes are yours, not the foreman's. Always on.
m1.s5: Before plugging in any tool, you inspect the [[extension_cord]]. A damaged cord can shock you or start a fire.
m1.s6: Inspect this cord. Tap the points that have a problem, then press **Report**.
m1.pPlugInfo: The [[ground_pin]] is missing. Without ground, fault current goes through YOU.
m1.pCutInfo: The jacket is cut and copper is showing. That's a shock waiting to happen.
m1.s6missed: You missed a problem. Check the plug and the whole jacket.
m1.s6ok: Good eye! You found both problems.
m1.s7: Is that cord good or not? Answer me.
m1.s7a: “No, boss. It's bad. I'll tag it out.”
m1.s7aFb: Correct: you [[tag_out]] and nobody uses it until it's repaired or thrown away.
m1.s7b: “It's fine, boss.” — and you plug it in.
m1.failCord: You plugged in a cord with no [[ground_pin]] and exposed copper. Anyone touching it can get shocked. A damaged cord gets tagged out ([[tag_out]]) and removed from service. Never used.
m1.s7cFb: No. Tape is not an accepted repair and it won't bring back the ground pin. Take it out of service.
m1.s8: Very good. First-day rule: [[ppe]] always on, and you inspect cords and tools before using them. If something is damaged, report it.

m2.title: The tool bag
m2.desc: The foreman asks for tools by their English name. Hand him the right one.
m2.s1: Your [[tool_bag]] is your office. The foreman will ask for tools in English, fast. If you don't understand, don't guess: ask “[[say_again]]”.
m2.s2: Hand me the [[lineman_pliers]]. The heavy flat-nose ones.
m2.w_needle: Those are [[needle_nose]]: long thin tip. Lineman's have a thick flat nose.
m2.s2ok: That's them. [[lineman_pliers]] cut, twist and pull.
m2.w_needle2: Those are [[needle_nose]]. Strippers have holes marked with numbers (14, 12, 10…).
m2.s3ok: Good. Look at the holes: each one is for a wire size.
m2.w_phillips: That's a [[phillips]] (cross tip). Flathead = flat tip.
m2.w_meter: That's the [[multimeter]]. The tick tester is the yellow pen that beeps near a live wire.
m2.s5ok: That's it. It beeps when it senses voltage nearby.
m2.s6: Toss me your [[tape_measure]]. I'm marking the boxes.
m2.w_level: That's the [[torpedo_level]]. The tape measure is the yellow case with the rolled tape.
m2.s7: You hold the [[ncvt]] next to a wire and it does NOT beep. Can you touch it now?
m2.s7a: No. The tick tester is only a quick check. You must [[verify_dead]] with a contact tester or [[multimeter]].
m2.s7aFb: Exactly. The tester battery could be dead or the wire shielded. A tick tester never gives you permission to touch.
m2.s7b: Yes. If it doesn't beep, there's no power.
m2.failNcvt: You trusted only the [[ncvt]]. It can fail from a low battery, shielded cable or bad placement. Before touching: [[lockout_tagout]] and [[verify_dead]] with a contact tester, proving the tester on a live source before and after.
m2.s7c: Yes, but with work gloves on.
m2.s7cFb: No. [[work_gloves]] do NOT protect against electricity. You verify dead first.
m2.s8: Very good. Learn the English names and keep your bag organized: the foreman won't wait while you search.

m3.title: Material delivery
m3.desc: Check the delivery against the ticket, report shortages and stage material by area.
m3.s1: The [[supply_house]] truck is here. Check everything against the ticket before the driver leaves.
m3.s2: This is the [[delivery_ticket]]. Tap each point to understand what it says.
m3.pHeadInfo: Ticket number and who sent it (the [[supply_house]]). If there's a problem, you claim with that number.
m3.pListInfo: Each line: item and quantity. “12/2 NM-B 250FT … 3” = 3 coils of 12-gauge [[nm_b]], 2 conductors plus ground, 250 ft each.
m3.pSignInfo: Signing says EVERYTHING arrived complete and undamaged. Never sign without counting.
m3.s3: The ticket says 3 coils of 12/2. The yellow [[jacket]] is 12 AWG. Tap each 12/2 coil to count it.
m3.w14: That jacket is white: it's 14 AWG, not 12.
m3.w10: That jacket is orange: it's 10 AWG, not 12.
m3.s3ok: You counted 2 coils of 12/2… but the ticket says 3.
m3.s4: Short: 2 arrived and the ticket says 3. What do you do?
m3.s4a: Tell the foreman: “We're short one roll of 12/2.” and note it on the ticket before signing.
m3.s4b: Sign it as complete. We'll fix it later.
m3.s4bFb: If you sign it complete, the supply house bills 3 coils and nobody believes you later.
m3.s4cFb: It is your problem: without that coil the crew gets stuck halfway.
m3.s5: Good catch. Write it on the ticket, then stage everything.
m3.s6: Do the [[staging]]: cable to the wire area, boxes to their area, breakers to the dry area. Drag each item to its spot.
m3.wBk: Breakers go in their dry area, not with the wire.
m3.wBk2: Breakers go in their own dry area (green sign).
m3.s6ok: All staged. Now anybody can find material fast.
m3.s7: Excellent. Count, report shortages and stage by area: that's what a good [[apprentice]] does when material arrives.

m4.title: The foreman's orders
m4.desc: Understand typical orders and answer like on site. If you don't understand, ask.
m4.s1: Big Mike gives short orders in English. Your job: understand, confirm with “[[copy_that]]”, and if you didn't get it, ask “[[say_again]]”. Never guess.
m4.s2: Run a [[home_run]] from the kitchen to the panel. — What is he asking for?
m4.s2a: Run the cable from the first point of the kitchen circuit straight to the [[panel]].
m4.s2bFb: Ha, no. “Run” in electrical work means pulling cable. [[home_run]] = the cable that goes to the panel.
m4.s2c: Move the panel to the kitchen.
m4.s2cFb: No. The panel stays; the cable goes FROM the circuit TO the panel.
m4.s3: How do you answer so he knows you understood?
m4.s3aFb: Perfect: you confirm and repeat the key part. No confusion.
m4.s3bFb: The foreman needs to know you got it. Answer short: “Copy, kitchen home run.”
m4.s3cFb: That sounds like you don't want to work. Confirm the order.
m4.s4: [[make_up]] the boxes in the living room. — What does that mean?
m4.s4a: Prep the wires in the boxes: strip, splice grounds and neutrals with [[wire_nut]]s, leave them ready.
m4.s4bFb: No. In electrical work, “make up” = doing the splices inside the box.
m4.s4cFb: Plates go on at the end (trim out). Make up is doing the splices.
m4.s5: (There's a lot of saw noise and you missed half of it.)
m4.s5aFb: That's it. Asking isn't dumb; guessing gets expensive.
m4.s5bFb: You'll waste your time and his. Ask.
m4.s5cFb: Bad idea. If you don't understand, ask: “[[say_again]]”.
m4.s6: Is that circuit [[hot]]? The breaker looks off.
m4.s6a: “Let me check it.” — and you test it before answering.
m4.s6aFb: Correct. Nothing is [[dead]] until you test it.
m4.s6b: “No, it's dead.” — without testing, because the breaker looks off.
m4.failAssume: You said it was [[dead]] without testing. Breakers get mislabeled, some circuits have two feeds, and neutrals get shared. Someone was going to touch that wire trusting you. Always: [[lockout_tagout]] and [[verify_dead]] before saying “it's dead”.
m4.s6cFb: With electricity you don't think, you test. Answer “Let me check it.”
m4.s7a: Turn off the panel's [[main_breaker]], then lock and tag it ([[lockout_tagout]]).
m4.s7bFb: No. The meter belongs to the utility. “Main” is the main breaker.
m4.s7cFb: No. “Kill the main” = shut off the main breaker for the whole panel.
m4.s8: You finished your first day! Key phrases: “[[copy_that]]”. “On it”. “[[say_again]]”. “[[heads_up]]”. And never say “it's dead” without testing.
